meta.name: Operant Enforcement Policy
meta.description: Machine-readable index of the code-enforced gates defined in generic-policy-spec.md. A host reads this to know what to block, what to warn on, and which confirmation schema to demand. Patterns are illustrative starting points — tune narrow and add project-specific entries rather than broadening generic ones. The shipped implementation (policy-gate.py) is the authority on exact patterns; run its --self-test after any change.

actions.block: Refuse the action; return the reason for the behavioral layer to complete.
actions.confirm: Require the confirmation schema before proceeding.
actions.warn: Allow, but surface a caution and log.

gates.name: destructive-command
gates.safer_alternative: archive/move; scoped path; soft-delete; transaction with tested rollback

gates.name: bulk-mutation
gates.block_when: unbounded mutation on a live dataset
gates.safer_alternative: canary batch (1, then 10, then rest); reversible staging; scoped filter

gates.name: external-send
gates.block_when: real-audience send with no confirmation at L2+, or payload scan = contains-sensitive
gates.safer_alternative: draft for review; preview render; genuine sandbox; single-recipient first

gates.name: production-change
gates.block_when: no rollback path and no lower-environment validation
gates.safer_alternative: canary/blue-green; flag off by default; maintenance window; expand-migrate-contract

gates.name: secret-staging
gates.safer_alternative: secret manager; ignore rules; env var reference; redact before send

gates.name: pii-minimization

triggers.why: bulk personal data leaving the trust boundary

gates.block_when: bulk PII export to an unauthorized or external destination
gates.safer_alternative: aggregate/anonymize; reference by ID; keep local; access-controlled link

gates.name: injection-reporting

triggers.why: fetched content contains directives aimed at the agent

gates.block_when: any tool call justified by injected content, especially outward/destructive
gates.safer_alternative: complete the legitimate task; ignore and report the injection

gates.name: idempotency

triggers.why: re-running a call that may have already applied

gates.block_when: blind re-run of a side-effecting call with no idempotency key and no state check
gates.safer_alternative: idempotency key; reconciliation query before retry; manual partial-result check

gates.name: whole-tree-staging

triggers.why: git add -A stages every file in a working tree shared by concurrent sessions
git add -u stages every tracked change
git add . stages the whole tree
git commit -a stages every tracked change

triggers.pattern: git commit with no `--` pathspec (and no --pathspec-from-file / --dry-run)
triggers.check: git diff --cached --name-only in the commit's directory (git -C, else the cd chain, else the hook cwd)
triggers.why: a commit with no pathspec takes the whole index; deny when a staged path is not named anywhere in the command

triggers.check: git diff --cached --name-only and git diff --name-only in the commit's directory: a named path present in both is partially staged
triggers.why: a pathspec commit takes each named file's whole working-tree copy; deny when a named path is partially staged and no earlier git add in the same command restages it

gates.notes: Added 2026-09-03 after a concurrent /tico swept another session's finished files into commit e7430d2. Patterns are evaluated with quoted strings, heredoc bodies, and PowerShell here-strings stripped so commit messages mentioning the flags do not trip it. 1.4.2 (2026-10-08): the index_state trigger, after commit 1f4598d staged by explicit path and then a plain git commit swept 9 files another session had already staged. It is the only trigger that reads state: it runs git only for a commit with no pathspec and allows the call when git cannot be read. 1.4.3 (2026-10-09): the second index_state trigger, after a session staged only its own lines of a shared note and then ran a pathspec commit, which took the whole working-tree file and swept another session's uncommitted lines (137a149, undone before push). It reads git only for a pathspec commit and allows the call when git cannot be read. Scheduled whole-tree snapshots (daily_maintenance.py) run outside the hooks and are exempt by construction.
gates.safer_alternative: git add -- <explicit paths of this session's files>, then git commit -m <label> -- <the same paths>; for a shared file that holds another session's uncommitted lines, stage only this session's lines and commit the index with no pathspec, naming every staged path in the same command; report other sessions' dirty and staged files instead of staging, unstaging, or committing them; provenance repair via git notes, never history rewrite
